text: Governance doesn't wait for an invitation. Two AI pilots are already running at LTV Global, and this lesson brings both of them under the program.

A generative-AI support assistant drafts replies from Beacon and Comet tickets. A forecasting model predicts SKU demand from Atlas orders. Neither waited for a strategy — which is exactly why Dana Whitfield asked Marcus Ibe to catch up now, before either reaches production.
Marcus applies five checks from this path's AI and Machine Learning Governance course: risk tier, data provenance, bias and fairness, model documentation, and a monitoring plan.

The forecasting model scores moderate risk. It trains on Orders and SKU — CDEs that already have owners and Lesson 7's quality gate behind them. It just needs a named monitoring owner and a written model card.

The support assistant scores high risk. It trains on two years of raw, unscrubbed tickets containing Confidential email addresses and occasional DateOfBirth mentions, with no owner and no monitoring plan defined.
Forecasting is close — add an owner and a model card. The assistant is blocked until its training data is scrubbed, an owner is named, and a human reviews every drafted reply before it's sent.
Next: Lesson 14 designs the architecture these models and every earlier deliverable actually run on.
